The losses total -$4,725 against +$307,929 in wins, and none were core NO-at-0.99 bets. 20 of 21 months up (worst month -$1). Max drawdown $17.7k (5% of profit); worst day -$13.4k; 87% of weeks up; top 5 days = 19% of profit. October 2025 crash month +$30k. In my fill sample every resolved market with z >= 1.5 won (67/67; 48/48 at z >= 3)
candidates.where_we_trade_it: Kalshi KXBTCMAXMON, KXBTCMINMON, KXETHMAXMON, KXETHMINMON (monthly one-touch, settled on a CF Benchmarks trimmed mean), plus annual KXBTCMAXY / KXBTCMINY / KXETHMAXY. Live check 2026-10-12: NO asks 0.96-0.99 at z 2.5-3.9 against a model fair value of 0.99-1.00 (about 1-3.5c of model edge), 49-2,099 contracts at the ask. No Polymarket US twin
candidates.why: The cleanest inferable rule on the boards: buy NO on a monthly touch strike when z >= ~2.5-3 and NO is priced below the one-touch fair value 1-2N(-z), then hold. Kalshi lists the same contract family, prices it the same way today and has depth. It needs no speed (positions last weeks) and works at 1-25 contracts; the fee is about 0.2c per contract at 0.97, rounded up per order. It is not a lock: it sells crash/spike insurance, one losing month wipes out roughly 30-50 wins, money is tied up for weeks, and the expected gain is only about 1-3% per position-month. My model is driftless and uses realized vol; crypto has fat tails and Kalshi settles on a trimmed mean, not Polymarket's Binance highs.

notes:
The best fit is the tail-selling rule shared by LucasMeow, x6916Cc00 and amis: buy NO on far strikes of monthly crypto touch ladders and hold. Kalshi lists the same contracts (KXBTCMAXMON etc.), prices them the same way today, it needs no speed and it works at $25. It is not a lock. Of everything I found, only complete-set or neg-risk merging comes close to riskless arbitrage, and I found no such opportunity the owner can run.

WHAT I DID (all read-only, keyless, public endpoints; scripts and data in /home/user/Claude/research/lab9/leaderboard/; raw/ is 916 MB and gitignored by research/lab9/.gitignore; nothing committed):
- Leaderboards. data-api.polymarket.com/v1/leaderboard works with timePeriod=all|month|week|day, orderBy=PNL, limit up to 50, offset, and category=crypto|weather|economics|finance|politics|sports|tech|culture|mentions; lb-api.polymarket.com/profit?window=all also works. I pulled overall all/month/week (top 200 each) and crypto/weather/economics/finance all/month/week (top 100 each): 1,278 unique wallets.
- Stage A, every wallet: the daily cumulative P&L series (user-pnl-api.polymarket.com/user-pnl?interval=all&fidelity=1d) and the newest 500 activity rows. Market families came from a slug classifier (classify.py). Output: stage_a.csv.
- Filter: mostly twin-able non-sports markets; active at least 120 days and within the last 30; profit over $20k; top 5 days under 50% of profit; max drawdown under 50% of profit; at least 60% of months up. 57 twin-able wallets and 20 sports wallets passed.
- Stage B, 46 wallets: newest 3,000 activity rows plus slices 7-240 days back, maker/taker split, 1,500 closed positions, open positions, Gamma market end dates, Coinbase hourly spot. Analyses: ladder z-scores and outcomes (ladder_rule.py) and weather bucket vs final high by local time (weather_side.py).
- Live Kalshi checks: the touch-ladder pricing above (kalshi_touch_now.py), and complete sets on 28 weather events (kalshi_set_arb.py): none cost less than $1 after fees.

MEASUREMENT CAVEATS:
- Win rates from closed-positions alone read too high, because many bots never redeem losing positions (one 15m bot had more than $69k of unredeemed losers). I used the P&L series for drawdown and consistency, and reported win rates only where unredeemed losers were small.
- Leaderboards only show survivors.
- The z-model is driftless lognormal on realized vol; implied vol and fat tails mean the 1-4c Kalshi 'edge' is partly a risk premium.

HONEST ON 'THE LOCK':
- Kalshi uses one YES/NO book per market, so YES ask + NO ask is always at least $1: there is no instant pair arbitrage there.
- Kalshi weather complete sets cost $1.01-1.15 after fees in the snapshot.
- The closest thing to true arbitrage seen was 0x496f76bd5cf4c2819c710ae90ed1c84b2dc6fa5d: Polymarket weather neg-risk / complete-set merging (569 MERGE + 137 CONVERSION in 6 hours), +$39.6k over 198 days, max drawdown $293. It relies on Polymarket's merge/convert, which Kalshi doesn't have.

EXCLUDED, WITH REASONS:
- 0xD9E0AACa (0xd9e0aaca471f489be338fd0f91a26e8669a805f2): sports market maker, +$1.63M over 612 days, 21 of 21 months up, max drawdown $2.7k, 95% maker, 18k fills a day. It needs fast in-play quotes; Polymarket US sports books are thin.
- BoneReader (0xd84c2b6d65dc596f49c7b6aadd6d74ca91e407b9): buys at >=0.97 a median 11 s AFTER 5m/15m windows close (already-decided outcomes). A speed play; Kalshi stops trading at close; it stopped in April 2026.
- mo-money (0x32ed2e546b187ca15e2841edc82b22c713cf8ec3): 89% maker on 5m/15m windows, median pair cost 1.02.
- rwo (0xd189664c5308903476f9f079820431e4fd7d06f4): 5m market maker, 19 of 20 months up, but only $26k in the last 90 days.
- Poligarch (0xb40e89677d59665d5188541ad860450a6e2a7cc9): weather market maker, +$207k over 408 days, max drawdown $3.8k, 91% maker, 42% US cities. The rule isn't clean.
- BeefSlayer (0x331bf91c132af9d921e1908ca0979363fc47193f): 90% Kalshi-live US cities, +$87k over 389 days, 11 of 14 months up, max drawdown $1.6k. It trades forecast-style across buckets, so no clean rule.
- uninfromedfloww, En111006, 0x29de3c62: late-window directional 15m taker bots.
- thanksforplayin and grasstoucher69: single-stock daily markets, no Kalshi twin.
- JnStrtPrdctnMrkts, Tokor, 0xf705fa, getbipped: concentrated in a few days or deep drawdowns.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEP: pre-register a paper test of the LucasMeow rule on Kalshi. Buy NO on KXBTCMAXMON / KXBTCMINMON / KXETHMAXMON / KXETHMINMON strikes when z >= 3 (30-day vol) and NO ask <= fair - 1c, at 10-25 contracts, hold to settlement. Check it on the history of past Polymarket monthly ladders (Gamma plus Binance highs) before risking real money.

candidates.where_we_trade_it: Kalshi KXHIGH*, KXLOWT*, KXRAIN after the lock: the decided side rests at the 0.99 tick, so the gross is 1% rather than 0.1%. Polymarket US tc-temp-*high: thin books (about 800-3,000 shares a side), and the lag after a lock is unmeasured because the venue publishes no trade history.
candidates.why: This is the only weather method that needs no speed. The public record shows it earns about nothing: margins of 0.03-0.07% on Polymarket international, and several wallets lost five figures, presumably because one bad resolution wipes out a thousand 0.1% wins. On Kalshi the 1-cent tick makes it 1% gross, with no maker fee and 0 violations in 243 locked brackets. But late orders queue behind 16.5k-115.5k contracts already resting at 0.99, so a $25 account would probably earn cents. It is honest to call this a near-riskless lock that is worth almost nothing.

notes:
BOTTOM LINE: I found no weather 'lock' that fits the owner. The consistent weather winners are all observation-reaction bots: they buy outcomes a fresh METAR has just decided, within seconds to about 2 minutes of the report. The lock itself is genuine: 0 of 243 METAR-locked Kalshi brackets settled against it, and HighTempTation won 99.6% of 4,358 markets. But on Kalshi the price is at the 0.99 tick within 5 minutes (rain: within 3), and Polymarket international reaches 0.997-0.999 even faster. A slow, small account is left with either about 1% gross at Kalshi's 0.99 tick, behind resting queues of 16.5k-115.5k contracts, or lottery-style longshot buying whose edge decayed in mid-2026.

VENUES:
- Kalshi Climate & Weather: 422 series; 57 with open markets today (2026-10-12). By 24h contracts: KXRAIN 873,950; KXHIGHLAX 240,132; KXHIGHMIA 156,185; KXHIGHNY 103,734; KXHIGHCHI 102,093; then HOU, ATL, BOS, AUS, PHIL, MIN, DC, PHX, SFO, DAL, DEN, OKC, SEA, NOLA, LV, SATX, SAN, TTN, EWR, SDF. The 24 KXHIGH* series total 1.06M; the 24 KXLOWT* total 138k; hourly KXTEMP* have under 1k.
- Kalshi settlement: 'maximum temperature recorded at <CLI site> according to The Weather Company' (weather.com/kalshi), i.e. the NWS daily climate report value, on a local-standard-time day. Last trade 11:59 PM local; expiry the next 7-8 AM ET. Stations: CLINYC Central Park, CLIMDW Midway, CLIMIA, CLILAX, CLIAUS Bergstrom, CLIDEN, CLIHOU Hobby, CLIDFW, and others.
- Fees: Kalshi fee_type is quadratic with multiplier 1, i.e. taker 0.07*p*(1-p) and no maker fee.
- Polymarket US has daily-high markets too: tc-temp-{nyc,mdw,mia,lax,sfo}high, 3,061 markets since 2026-04-22. They settle on the NWS CLI at the same stations as Kalshi, with fee coefficient 0.0695. A snapshot of 30 matching Oct-13 brackets showed quotes within about 1c of Kalshi and no cross-venue arbitrage (best net -0.17c after fees). It has no public trade history, so its lag after a lock is unmeasured.
- Polymarket international resolves on the NOAA timeseries (METAR), often at other stations: LaGuardia, O'Hare, Love Field, Buckley. The same station is used for MIA, LAX, AUS, HOU, ATL, SEA, SFO.
- The CLI max equals the METAR max or exceeds it by 1-2F, never less (NY +1 on 12 of 21 days; CHI +1 11/21 and +2 1/21; MIA +1 12/21 and +2 3/21). So locks transfer safely, but nowcast rules must account for the offset.

HOW MEASURED: The weather leaderboard (data-api /v1/leaderboard?category=WEATHER works; lb-api /profit also answers) gave the pool. 167,893 resolved weather markets came from gamma. Records are per-market cash-flow ledgers built from /activity. They match the leaderboard within about 1-5% for HighTempTation, Weatherstappen, BeefSlayer and badatmath. Do not use /closed-positions for wallets that split or merge: it gave badatmath. +$552k against a ledger +$65k and leaderboard +$68k. One gap is unresolved: HondaCivic is ledger +$244k against leaderboard +$68.6k (a lock-style bot at about 0.99, inactive since June). Market makers were excluded: badatmath. (+$65k incl. $18.4k rewards, max DD $18.3k), opopv. (+$68k, of which $42.6k rewards) and ColdMath. Lock and timing checks compare each buy to the IEM METAR archive; whether an outcome was decided by observations matched the real resolution in 7,153 of 7,172 checked buys.
